input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the \"Deerskin\" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is a non-compete/field-of-use restriction binding us (the Company): it bars us from participating in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" (open-ended, extending to unnamed "companies similar to" the named retailers), and it hands HDI an exclusive right in our own "Deerskin" brand, which prevents us from using or licensing our own brand. It therefore fails the preferred position and also fails fallback on material terms: the scope is not a single named competing product, and there is no carve-out for our internal development or for acquisitions (the only carve-out, Section 6.2, is limited to closeout merchandise). Duration is term-only, which is the one fallback element already satisfied. HDI's own covenant in Section 6.3 binds the vendor and is unaffected. We take the preferred position and remove the restriction and the brand exclusivity, offering the narrowed fallback in the comment.

ops.newText: 6.1 The Company may participate in any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or any other products, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products we offer or the projects we run, and we cannot grant HDI an exclusive right in our own "Deerskin" brand, so we have replaced Section 6.1 with an express confirmation that no such restriction applies to us; our retained right in 6.2 and HDI's covenant in 6.3 are unaffected. If HDI needs protection, we could consider a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Remove the Section 6.1 non-compete and brand exclusivity binding the Company

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
